lens: What unstated assumption is load-bearing in this artefact?

findings.title: R9/AC-7c stub-section fallback assumes a 019 absorption contract that is not stated anywhere
findings.claim: R9 plus AC-7c declare that until 019-per-task-manifest lands, 017 writes the three markers into a `## Per-task manifest stub` section appended at the bottom of `{NNN-slug}-tasks.md`, and that 019 will 'absorb the section when it lands by promoting the stub to its own per-task manifest file'. The absorption contract — schema shape 019 expects, deterministic locator, migration semantics, what happens to the appended stubs after 019 promotes them — is load-bearing for the marker-schema-stays-stable claim, but lives nowhere: not in 019's brief, not in this PRD beyond a one-line aspiration, not in the decision log. The assumption that 019 will accept this exact stub-section heading and the exact three-line schema is unstated AND unverifiable at PRD-gate time.
evidence: PRD R9 schema-dependency clause (`prd.md:87`): '019 absorbs the section when it lands by promoting the stub to its own per-task manifest file. The marker schema (the three-line block above) is owned by 017; 019 reads the schema unchanged.'

AC-7c (`prd.md:127`): mandates verbatim heading `## Per-task manifest stub` 'so 019 can locate and absorb it deterministically' — but no 019 spec is cited and the absorption contract is not written down.
Interview Round 4 (`interview.md:45`): names the per-task manifest as '019, future' — confirms 019 is unbuilt; therefore its absorption contract cannot exist yet.
Decision log: no entry covering the 017↔019 schema handoff.
findings.tradeoff: Option A (status quo) — ship 017 with the stub fallback and trust that 019 will be designed around it. Risk: if 019's design surfaces a schema mismatch (e.g. needs additional fields for retrospect synthesis, needs per-task files not a per-feature appendix), the stub heading becomes legacy noise and 017's manifest-marker contract drifts. Option B (recommended) — add an explicit assumption in PRD Open Questions naming the 017→019 schema handoff as the load-bearing dependency, AND mandate that 019's PRD cite 017's R9 marker schema verbatim before 019 closes Gate 2. Option C — defer R9's marker-line shape to 019 entirely; 017 only mandates the cycle, not the marker syntax. This narrows 017's surface but loses the auditability hook 017 explicitly claims.
findings.proposed_change: Add to PRD Open Questions: 'The 017→019 stub-absorption contract is asserted in R9/AC-7c but not specified anywhere. Decision needed before 017 ships to dogfood: (a) lock the absorption contract here and require 019's PRD to cite 017's R9 schema verbatim, or (b) drop AC-7c and defer the marker-line shape to 019.' Alternatively, add an Assumption block immediately after R9 stating: 'This PRD assumes 019 will adopt 017's three-line marker schema unchanged and use the verbatim `## Per-task manifest stub` heading as its locator. If 019's design surfaces a different schema, R9 + AC-7c re-open.'

findings.title: R6 'strong CI signal' is the load-bearing concept gating the tddRequired opt-out and is never operationally defined
findings.claim: R6's 'Serves goal' line and the interview Round 1 trace both lean on the phrase 'projects with strong CI signal' as the justification for `tddRequired: false`. The phrase is never defined: no test-coverage threshold, no flake-rate ceiling, no runner-output contract, no green-build-discipline metric. A project operator considering whether to flip `tddRequired: false` has nothing to check against — the decision becomes vibes-based, which is exactly what TDD discipline is meant to replace. The assumption that operators can self-assess 'strong CI signal' is load-bearing because it determines whether the opt-out is principled or a loophole.
evidence: PRD R6 trace (`prd.md:67`): 'Projects with strong CI signal and binary-AC-heavy task lists may opt out for Green tasks where the test plan would be redundant with the AC itself.'
PRD R6 Serves goal (`prd.md:68`): 'the configurable knob respects projects with strong CI signal without forcing TDD universally.'
Interview Round 1 (`interview.md:27`): same phrase, no definition.

No reference in `CORE_PRINCIPLES.md`, `rules/guidelines.md`, `rules/non-negotiable.md`, or `admin/environment.json` schema to a 'CI signal strength' check; nothing in `admin/config.json` schema validates the precondition before allowing `tddRequired: false`.
findings.tradeoff: Option A (status quo) — ship the knob with the soft justification and rely on operator judgment. Risk: the knob becomes a way to silently disable TDD; the audit trail captures `red: skipped (config)` but not whether the skip was principled. Option B — add a concrete CI-signal definition (e.g. 'CI runs `vitest`, `typecheck`, and `lint` on every PR; merge requires all three green; coverage report shows ≥80% on touched files') and require the precondition before `tddRequired: false` is honored. Option C — drop the phrase from the PRD entirely and reframe R6 as 'projects may opt out at their own risk; the manifest captures the choice'. Honest but loses the principled-opt-out framing.
findings.proposed_change: Add a definition block to R6: 'Strong CI signal, for the purposes of this knob, means: (a) every PR runs vitest + typecheck + lint as required checks, (b) merge is blocked on red checks, (c) the project enforces a binary-AC convention in PRDs (every AC has a binary pass/fail criterion). The skill does not validate the precondition; the operator self-attests by setting `tddRequired: false` and the manifest records the attestation alongside `red: skipped (config)`.' OR add to Open Questions: 'R6 leans on `strong CI signal` as the justification but does not define it. Lock a definition before 017 ships, or accept that the knob is operator-trust-based.'

findings.title: R10 + AC-8 assume Phase E reviewers do not see the per-task manifest, but the existing develop skill loads a per-task manifest scaffold into context at Phase B and AC-8's grep test will false-positive on existing manifest references
findings.claim: R10 asserts Phase E reviewers 'do not read the markers and the manifest is not in their context'. AC-8 verifies this by 'absence of "red marker", "green marker", "refactor marker", "manifest" string occurrences in the Phase E and Phase F body ranges'. Two unstated assumptions: (1) the existing `develop/SKILL.md:115` already names 'per-task manifest scaffold' as a context-budget input — the manifest concept is already in develop's context plumbing, so the claim that Phase E reviewers do not see it requires an explicit input-list contract for Phase E reviewers, not just absence of grep matches; (2) AC-8's grep for the literal string 'manifest' in Phase E/F bodies will false-positive on lines like `debate-log/develop-gate5/manifest.md` (Phase E itself produces a Gate 5 manifest) and on Phase E.7 closer headings — making AC-8 untestable as written. The assumption that grep-on-'manifest' produces a clean signal is load-bearing for AC-8's binary verification and is wrong.
evidence: Existing `develop/SKILL.md:115`: 'measure the actually-loaded context size for the task's payload (PRD slice + task spec + matched lessons + per-task manifest scaffold + codebase-context files + test plan)' — the per-task manifest is already a named context input at Phase B.
Existing `develop/SKILL.md:296,495`: Phase E.6 and E.7 reference `debate-log/develop-gate5/manifest.md` — AC-8's grep for 'manifest' will match these unconditionally.

PRD AC-8 (`prd.md:130`): 'Verified by absence of "red marker", "green marker", "refactor marker", "manifest" string occurrences in the Phase E and Phase F body ranges' — wholly fails on existing Phase E body.
PRD R10 (`prd.md:89`): 'Phase E's reviewer agents do not read the markers and the manifest is not in their context' — no operational verification mechanism specified beyond AC-8.
findings.tradeoff: Option A (status quo) — leave AC-8 as a grep test. Result: AC-8 is un-passable on the current develop skill body without removing existing 'manifest.md' references that have nothing to do with 017's markers. Option B — narrow AC-8 to a positive-input-list test: 'Phase E.3 reviewer dispatch passes only the code diff, the per-task plan, the task entry, and the reviewer role definition; the per-task manifest (R9 scaffold) is not in the dispatch payload list.' This is both verifiable (re-read the bullet list at Phase E.3) and accurate to R10's intent. Option C — drop R10 entirely; let Phase E reviewers see the markers; downside is exactly what R10 was meant to prevent (cycle structure leaking into the dumb-zone).
findings.proposed_change: Replace AC-8's grep test with a structural test against Phase E.3's reviewer-dispatch input list: 'AC-8. Phase E.3 reviewer-dispatch input list (the four bullets passed to each forked reviewer sub-agent in `develop/SKILL.md`) does NOT include the per-task manifest, the marker stub section, or the `{NNN-slug}-tasks.md` per-task-manifest-stub appendix. Phase E reviewers see only the code diff, the per-task plan, the tasks-file entry, and their own role definition.' Drop the grep-on-manifest test (false positives on Gate 5's own manifest.md). Add a complementary AC: 'AC-8b. Phase B context-budget input list (`develop/SKILL.md:115`) is amended so the `per-task manifest scaffold` line either (a) explicitly excludes the R9 marker stub from the Phase E reviewer payload, or (b) renames the scaffold to clarify it is a Phase D input only.'

findings.title: AC-2's literal invocation `specflow:test {NNN-slug} --plan-only --task T{N}` mixes template literal with grep-test verbatim — unstated assumption about how AC-2 verifies
findings.claim: AC-2 says the develop skill body 'contains the literal invocation `specflow:test {NNN-slug} --plan-only --task T{N}`'. The braces `{NNN-slug}` and `T{N}` are template placeholders that develop substitutes at runtime per task. The unstated assumption is whether AC-2 is satisfied by the literal placeholder string in the prose (the SKILL.md is a template, so this is plausible) or by a runtime invocation log. If the former, the test passes trivially the moment the prose mentions the bash line. If the latter, AC-2 needs a fixture and a runtime trace. The PRD does not say which.
evidence: PRD AC-2 (`prd.md:106`): 'sub-phase D.1 (Red) body contains the literal invocation `specflow:test {NNN-slug} --plan-only --task T{N}`'
Develop SKILL.md uses placeholder convention `{NNN-slug}` throughout (`develop/SKILL.md:52,83,409`), confirming this is template prose — but AC-2's intent is not stated.
Other ACs (e.g. AC-1 with explicit grep regex `^### D\.[123]`) name their verification mechanism; AC-2 does not.
findings.tradeoff: Option A — explicitly say AC-2 is a grep against the SKILL.md prose (low-cost, unambiguous). Option B — require both the prose mention AND a runtime invocation fixture under examples/ that demonstrates the placeholder substitution working. Option B catches the 'prose says it but the substitution mechanism never runs' failure mode the AC-7a/7b worked example already partially addresses.
findings.proposed_change: Add to AC-2: 'Verified via grep `specflow:test \{NNN-slug\} --plan-only --task T\{N\}` against `plugins/specflow/skills/develop/SKILL.md` Phase D.1 body — the literal template placeholder string, not a substituted invocation.'

findings.title: R8 + AC-6 assume `specflow:test --plan-only --task T{N}` runs without firing test/SKILL.md Phase B.5's user-prompt — but B.5 requires a `continue|revise|skip` answer mid-flow
findings.claim: R8 says the Red sub-phase fires `specflow:test --plan-only --task T{N}` to write the failing test plan. The existing `test/SKILL.md` Phase B.5 (`test/SKILL.md:200-214`) inserts a Codex adversarial pass and a user-input prompt (`continue | revise: ... | skip`) before reporting in `--plan-only` mode. The assumption that this prompt fits inside develop's single-context-window contract — without breaking the 029 doctrine of no-mid-task-compaction and no-cross-session-resumption — is unstated. Worse, the prompt is a synchronous user-interaction inside what 017 frames as an automated Red sub-phase: the engineer is paired-HITL on Yellow tasks already, but Phase B.5's prompt is a *test-skill* user prompt fired from inside develop's Red phase, which compounds prompt fatigue.
evidence: PRD R8 (`prd.md:74`): 'Extend `test/SKILL.md` `--plan-only` mode … with the additional `--task T{N}` flag it writes the per-task plan section into `{NNN-slug}-test.md`'
Existing `test/SKILL.md:200-214` Phase B.5: synchronous Codex pass + 'Reply `continue` to proceed, `revise: <description>` … or `skip`'
PRD R1 (`prd.md:46`): names the Red invocation as `specflow:test {NNN-slug} --plan-only --task T{N}` — does not address the embedded user prompt.
Existing `develop/SKILL.md:401`: '029 single-context-window per task' contract — synchronous external-skill prompts inside this window are not addressed.
findings.tradeoff: Option A — leave the assumption implicit. Risk: a Yellow-lane Red sub-phase with `--plan-only --task T{N}` blocks for user input on Codex's pre-execution review; the engineer is already paired-HITL, but now sees a second prompt from inside Red, before they get to Green. Option B — declare in R8 that `--task T{N}` mode skips Phase B.5 (the Codex adversarial pass for the per-task slice is deferred to Phase E's Codex reviewer, which already exists). Option C — declare that Phase B.5 fires once at the feature level and the per-task `--task T{N}` invocations skip B.5 because the feature-level pass already covered the test plan. Option B is simpler and tighter to the 'one prompt per phase' principle.
findings.proposed_change: Add an explicit clause to R8: 'When `--task T{N}` is supplied in `--plan-only` mode, `test/SKILL.md` Phase B.5 (Codex adversarial pass + user prompt) is skipped — the per-task slice inherits whatever B.5 outcome the feature-level test plan recorded, and Gate 5's Codex reviewer covers cross-provider concerns at code-vs-plan time.' Alternatively, add to Open Questions: 'R8's `--plan-only --task T{N}` invocation enters `test/SKILL.md` Phase B.5 (Codex pass + user prompt) by default. Decide before shipping: (a) skip B.5 in per-task mode, (b) keep B.5 and accept the extra prompt inside Red, (c) re-shape B.5 to feature-level-only.'

summary: Three load-bearing unstated assumptions block PRD-gate close: (1) R9/AC-7c assert a 017→019 stub-absorption contract that exists nowhere; (2) R6's `strong CI signal` justification for the tddRequired opt-out is never operationalised; (3) R10/AC-8 conflict with the existing develop skill's manifest-scaffold context input AND AC-8's grep test will false-positive on Gate 5's own manifest.md references. Two concerns: AC-2's verification mechanism is ambiguous (template placeholder vs runtime trace), and R8 silently inherits test/SKILL.md Phase B.5's user-prompt inside develop's Red sub-phase, breaching the 029 single-context-window discipline 017 is meant to enforce.
